title: Zagwe dynasty
capsule: The Zagwe were an Agaw-speaking Christian dynasty that ruled the northern Ethiopian highlands from a capital at Roha (later renamed Lalibela), succeeding the Aksumite kingdom and maintaining Chalcedonian Christian rule through a succession of priest-kings. Their most celebrated monarch, Gebre Meskel Lalibela (r. c. 1181–1221), commissioned eleven monolithic rock-hewn churches at Roha — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and major pilgrimage centre equated by Ethiopian tradition with Jerusalem. In 1270, Yekuno Amlak overthrew the last Zagwe ruler and claimed Solomonic descent, founding the dynasty that would rule Ethiopia until 1974.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Zagwe heartland in Lasta is reasonably well attested through Ethiopian chronicles and UNESCO heritage surveys of the Lalibela churches, but peripheral territorial extent remains uncertain due to limited contemporary documentation.
